Fix a cohort \(s\) and condition throughout on a value of \(z_0\) for which the two query-conditional design assumptions hold.  Since \(0<\lambda\le1\), the order convention gives \(r=0\), so \(G_{sT}(z_{0s},b)\) is scalar.  By continuity of \(K\) and its positivity near zero, there are \(k_0>0\) and \(\eta\in(0,1)\) such that \(K(v)\ge k_0\) for \(\|v\|_2\le\eta\).  Decrease \(\eta\), if necessary, so that the ball \(B(z_{0s},\eta b)\) lies in \([0,1]^d\) for every \(0<b\le1\).  The replacement of \texttt{ass:design-density} then gives, uniformly in \(t\),
\[
 p_{tb}:=\Pr\{\|X_{st}-z_{0s}\|_2\le\eta b\mid z_0\}
 \ge c_Xv_d\eta^db^d=:c_pb^d.
\tag{1}
\]
If \(M_b\) counts these visits, the definition of the local-constant Gram matrix gives
\[
 G_{sT}(z_{0s},b)\ge \frac{k_0M_b}{Tb^d}.
\tag{2}
\]

We next establish a conditional occupancy bound using only the conditional design mixing assumption.  Let
\[
 a=\left\lceil\frac{3\log(T\vee2)}{|\log\rho_0|}\right\rceil.
\]
Partition the calendar into consecutive blocks of length \(a\), and separate the complete blocks according to parity.  Two successive blocks in either parity are separated by at least \(a\) indices.  From the total-variation definition of beta mixing, an induction replacing the retained blocks one at a time by independent variables with the same conditional block marginals changes the probability of any event by at most the sum of the intervening conditional beta coefficients.  Over both parities this error is at most
\[
 2\left\lceil\frac{T}{a}\right\rceil\beta_0\rho_0^a
 \le CT^{-2}.
\tag{3}
\]
This coupling concerns only the design blocks and uses the replacement of \texttt{ass:temporal-mixing}; no response block is conditioned upon or decoupled.

For an independent comparison block let \(Y_j\in[0,a]\) be its number of visits.  Convexity of \(y\mapsto e^{-y/a}\) on \([0,a]\) gives the chord bound
\[
 \mathbb E(e^{-Y_j/a}\mid z_0)
 \le1-\frac{1-e^{-1}}a\mathbb E(Y_j\mid z_0)
 \le\exp\{-c b^d\},
\tag{4}
\]
where the last inequality uses (1).  Exponential Markov applied to the product of the comparison blocks, separately for the two parities, and then (3), yields constants \(c_1,C_1>0\) such that
\[
 \Pr\{M_b\le c_1Tb^d\mid z_0\}
 \le C_1\exp\{-c_1Tb^d/a\}+C_1T^{-2}
\tag{5}
\]
whenever \(Tb^d\ge C_1a\).  Enlarging \(C_1\) makes (5) a valid trivial bound at smaller scales.  The stipulated compatibility of \(c_G\) with the population local-constant Gram lower bound ensures that (2) is at least \(c_G\) on the complement of the event in (5).

Put
\[
 b_\circ=(Tn_s)^{-1/(2\lambda+d)}\vee N^{-1/2}
          \vee(a/T)^{1/d}.
\tag{6}
\]
The smallest grid point not below any number in \([b_{0s},1]\) is at most twice that number.  Apply (5) successively at dyadic grid points of order \(2^jb_\circ\).  A union bound over the remaining larger grid points gives
\[
 \Pr\{h_s^\star>C2^jb_\circ\mid z_0\}
 \le C\exp(-c2^{jd})+CT^{-2},\qquad j\ge0,
\tag{7}
\]
until the scale reaches one; beyond one the probability is zero.  For the finitely many values for which \(b_\circ\) is bounded away from zero, the claimed moment bound follows directly from \(h_s^\star\le1\), after enlarging \(C\).  Dyadic summation of (7) otherwise gives
\[
 \mathbb E\{(h_s^\star)^{2\lambda}\mid z_0\}
 \le Cb_\circ^{2\lambda}+CT^{-2}.
\tag{8}
\]
Since \(a\le C\log(T\vee2)\) and \(2\lambda/d\le2\), (6)--(8) imply
\[
 \mathbb E\{(h_s^\star)^{2\lambda}\mid z_0\}
 \le C\left\{(Tn_s)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}+N^{-\lambda}
 +\left(\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right)^{2\lambda/d}\right\}.
\tag{9}
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz gives the asserted first-moment version.

At \(b=1\), (1)--(5) imply
\[
 \Pr\{G_{sT}(z_{0s},1)<c_G\mid z_0\}\le CT^{-2}.
\]
Whenever this inequality fails for no cohort, \((z_{0s},1)\) belongs to every fold--cohort anchor set, so \(\mathsf F_{\mathrm{fb}}\) cannot occur.  A union bound over the fixed number \(S\) of cohorts proves
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}
 \Pr_P(\mathsf F_{\mathrm{fb}}\mid z_0)\le CT^{-2}.
\tag{10}
\]
For \(P\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm{iid}}_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), the comparison blocks are already independent conditional on \(z_0\).  Taking \(a=1\) in (5)--(9) replaces the last term in (9) by \(T^{-2\lambda/d}\).  This proves every assertion using only query-conditional design regularity.

Put \(q=Sd\) and
\[
 A=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s},
 \qquad D_X=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\rho_{sX}(z_{0s})^\lambda.
\tag{1}
\]
We first work in the deterministic experiment \(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\).  Fix \(\xi=(\mathbb Q_\xi;\mu,f,z)\).  Conditional on the donor sample, define
\[
 U_{si}=E_{si}-\mu_s-K_N^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K_N}
 \{Q_{s,t_{s\ell},i}-f_s(X_{s,t_{s\ell}})\}.
\tag{2}
\]
The experiment definition makes the donor sample independent of all unit histories, and makes those histories independent across \((s,i)\).  Thus the variables in (2) are conditionally centered and independent across \((s,i)\).  Since \(|E_{si}|\vee|Q_{sti}|\vee|\mu_s|\vee\|f_s\|_\infty\le B\), one has \(|U_{si}|\le4B\), and hence
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{\mathbb Q_\xi}\!\left(
 \sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}U_{si}
 \mathrel{\Big|}(Z_j)_j\right)\le16B^2A.
\tag{3}
\]

Let \(t_s^0\) be the smallest nearest design index to \(z_{0s}\).  Twice applying the triangle inequality and using the definition of \(t_{s\ell}\) gives
\[
 \|X_{s,t_{s\ell}}-z_s\|_2
 \le\rho_{sX}(z_{0s})+\|z_s-z_{0s}\|_2
      +2\|\widetilde z_{\ell s}-z_s\|_2.
\tag{4}
\]
Because \(0<\lambda\le1\), powers of order \(\lambda\) are subadditive.  The Holder restriction and (4) yield
\[
 |f_s(X_{s,t_{s\ell}})-f_s(z_s)|
 \le C\{\rho_{sX}(z_{0s})^\lambda+\|z_s-z_{0s}\|_2^\lambda
          +\|\widetilde z_{\ell s}-z_s\|_2^\lambda\}.
\tag{5}
\]
Projection onto the cube is nonexpansive, each balanced donor fold has size at least \(N/3\), and the covariance restriction gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}\|\widetilde z_\ell-z\|_2^2
 \le\frac{\operatorname{tr}(\Sigma)}{|I_\ell|}
 \le\frac{3qC_\Sigma}{N}.
\tag{6}
\]
The experiment also imposes \(\|z-z_0\|_2^2\le C_\Sigma/N\).  Expanding \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{opt}}-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\) into the centered sum in (3) and the approximation errors in (5), then applying Jensen's inequality to (6), proves
\[
 \sup_{\xi\in\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}
 \{\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{opt}}-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\}^2
 \le C\{A+D_X^2+N^{-\lambda}\}
 \le CR_{X,\mathrm{opt}}.
\tag{7}
\]
The last inequality is \texttt{lem:rough-holder-optimal-recovery-geometry}.  Since \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{opt}}\) is measurable from the observations, the first minimax inequality follows.

For later use, we derive an elementary two-law bound.  If laws \(P_0,P_1\) have targets separated by \(\Delta\) and total variation at most \(1-\eta\), then, with \(A_0=\{|\widetilde\theta-\theta_0|<\Delta/2\}\), the triangle inequality and the variational definition of total variation give
\[
 \max_{v=0,1}\mathbb E_v(\widetilde\theta-\theta_v)^2
 \ge\frac{\Delta^2}{8}\{P_0(A_0^c)+P_1(A_0)\}
 \ge\frac{\eta\Delta^2}{8}.
\tag{8}
\]

For the treated-mean channel, keep the response and donor coordinates fixed and, under \(v\in\{-1,1\}\), take the \(E_{si}\)'s independently in \(\{-b,b\}\), where \(0<b<B\), with
\[
 \Pr_v(E_{si}=b)=\frac12+v\varepsilon_s,
 \qquad \varepsilon_s=\frac{\gamma\pi_s}{bn_s\sqrt A}.
\tag{9}
\]
Because \(A\ge\pi_s^2/n_s\), a sufficiently small fixed \(\gamma\) puts every probability in \([1/4,3/4]\).  The targets differ by \(4\gamma\sqrt A\).  The Hellinger affinity of the two product laws is
\[
 \prod_{s=1}^{S}(1-4\varepsilon_s^2)^{n_s/2}
 \ge\exp(-C\gamma^2/b^2)>0,
\tag{10}
\]
because \(\sum_s n_s\varepsilon_s^2=\gamma^2/b^2\).  If \(p_-\) and \(p_+\) are their densities, Cauchy--Schwarz applied to \(|p_+-p_-|=|\sqrt{p_+}-\sqrt{p_-}|(\sqrt{p_+}+\sqrt{p_-})\) gives
\[
 \|P_+-P_-\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le\left\{1-\left(\int\sqrt{p_+p_-}\right)^2\right\}^{1/2}<1.
\]
Equations (8)--(10) therefore give risk at least \(cA\).

For the fixed-design channel, choose
\[
 q_s(x)=a_0\min_{1\le t\le T}\|x-X_{st}\|_2^\lambda
\]
with \(a_0>0\) sufficiently small in terms of \(B,L,d\), and put \(f_s=q_s/2\), \(g_s=-q_s/2\).  Distance to a finite set is one-Lipschitz and \(|u^\lambda-v^\lambda|\le|u-v|^\lambda\); hence these surfaces are in the required Holder ball and are bounded by \(B\).  They agree at every design site.  Deterministic zero responses, identical event laws, and identical donors centered at \(z_0\) therefore produce identical observed laws, whereas the targets differ by
\[
 \sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_sq_s(z_{0s})=a_0D_X.
\tag{11}
\]
Equation (8) gives risk at least \(cD_X^2\).

For the donor channel assume the strict interior and moment slack in the theorem.  Apply \texttt{lem:full-covariance-location-pair} with any fixed \(\eta\in(0,1)\).  Its displacement has a single nonzero coordinate, belonging to some cohort \(s_0\); write that coordinate as \(x_k\).  Use the same regression under both laws,
\[
 f_{s_0}(x)=a_1|x_k-z_{0,s_0k}|^\lambda,
 \qquad f_s(x)=0\quad(s\ne s_0),
\tag{12}
\]
where \(a_1>0\) is small enough for boundedness and Holder radius \(L\).  Keep all response and event laws identical.  The two targets then differ by at least \(cN^{-\lambda/2}\), while the product total variation is at most \(1-\eta\).  Equation (8) yields risk at least \(cN^{-\lambda}\).  Taking the maximum of the treated, fixed-design, and donor lower bounds and applying \texttt{lem:rough-holder-optimal-recovery-geometry} proves
\[
 cR_{X,\mathrm{opt}}(z_0,\Sigma)
 \le\inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{\xi\in\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_\xi}
 \{\widetilde\tau-\theta_{\mathfrak E}(\xi)\}^2.
\tag{13}
\]

We now prove the causal bridge.  Let \(\mathcal X\) be generated by the exact design, \(\mathcal H\) by all unit histories, and \(\mathcal Z\) by the donors.  Assumption \texttt{ass:donor-training-separation} says that \(\mathcal Z\) is conditionally independent of \(\mathcal X\vee\mathcal H\) given \(z_0\).  Thus, for bounded \(\mathcal Z\)-measurable \(U\) and bounded \(\mathcal H\)-measurable \(V\), conditional factorization and the tower property give
\[
 \mathbb E(UV\mid z_0,\mathcal X)
 =\mathbb E(U\mid z_0)\mathbb E(V\mid z_0,\mathcal X)
 \quad\text{almost surely}.
\tag{14}
\]
Together with \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering}, cross-unit independence, boundedness, and the donor moment conditions, (14) shows that the observed conditional kernel with its labels belongs to \(\mathfrak E_X(z_0,\Sigma)\) for \(P\)-almost every \(X\).  No version is chosen at a null design.  Lemma \texttt{lem:causal-identification} equates its statistical target with \(\tau(z_0)\), so (7) proves the asserted conditional causal upper bound.

If each cohort design contains \(z_{0s}\), then \(D_X=0\), and the exact-site conclusion follows from \texttt{lem:rough-holder-optimal-recovery-geometry}.  Finally suppose \(g_{sT}(z_0)<1\) for every \(s\).  Then \((z_{0s},h_s^\star)\) is feasible in every foldwise anchor search.  Certificate optimality gives
\[
\begin{split}
 &C_H\|\widehat u_{s\ell}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\lambda
 +C_H\widehat h_{s\ell}^\lambda
 +C_V(Tn_s\widehat h_{s\ell}^d)^{-1/2}\\
 &\quad\le C_H\|z_{0s}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\lambda
 +C_H(h_s^\star)^\lambda
 +C_V\{Tn_s(h_s^\star)^d\}^{-1/2}.
\end{split}
\tag{15}
\]
The bandwidth floor makes the last term no larger than \((h_s^\star)^\lambda\).  Since \(r=0\), the actual averaged fit has nonnegative weights summing to one.  Holder continuity bounds its approximation bias by the first two terms on the left of (15), while conditional cross-unit independence bounds the variance of the resulting within-unit contrasts by \(CA\).  Donor unbiasedness, (6) with \(z=z_0\), Jensen's inequality, and (15) therefore yield
\[
 \mathbb E_P[\{\widehat\tau-\tau(z_0)\}^2\mid z_0,(X_{st})]
 \le CR_D.
\tag{16}
\]
The last assertion of \texttt{lem:rough-holder-optimal-recovery-geometry} gives \(R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\le CR_D\).  No converse based on the Gram certificate is used.

Write
\[
 A=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s},
 \qquad D_T=\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}^{2\lambda/d}.
\tag{1}
\]
On the event that every reference anchor is coercive, the conditional comparison in (15)--(16) of \texttt{thm:conditional-frontier} applies.  On its complement, both \(\widehat\tau\) and \(\tau(z_0)\) lie in \([-2B,2B]\), so squared error is at most \(16B^2\).  The query-conditional occupancy result \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-anchor-moment} bounds the complement's conditional probability by \(CT^{-2}\).  Minkowski's inequality and both moment bounds in that lemma give
\[
\begin{split}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}
 \mathbb E_P[\{\widehat\tau-\tau(z_0)\}^2\mid z_0]
 \le C\bigg[&A+
 \left\{\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s(Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\right\}^2\\
 &+D_T+N^{-\lambda}\bigg]
 \le CR_\star.
\end{split}
\tag{2}
\]
Here \(T^{-2}\le CD_T\), because \(0<2\lambda/d\le2\).  The donor-versus-panel factorization needed by the conditional comparison is equation (14) of \texttt{thm:conditional-frontier}.

The smoothing display is redundant.  With \(a_s=n_s^{-1/2}\) and \(b=T^{-\lambda/d}\), exponent arithmetic gives
\[
 (Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
 =a_s^{2\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}b^{d/(2\lambda+d)}
 \le a_s\vee b.
\tag{3}
\]
Since \(S\) is fixed, Cauchy--Schwarz implies
\[
 \left\{\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s(Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}\right\}^2
 \le2S\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}+2T^{-2\lambda/d}
 \le C(A+D_T).
\tag{4}
\]

Assume now \(\delta_0<1/2\) and \(B^4>(Sd)^2\).  For the treated-mean lower channel, take query-conditionally independent uniform exact designs, a common admissible donor law independent of the complete panel, and constant untreated surfaces.  Embed the two event-outcome laws in (9)--(10) of \texttt{thm:conditional-frontier}, translated into a fixed positive subinterval of \((-B,B)\).  Set treated potential wealth equal to the observed outcome and untreated event wealth equal to the constant surface.  With positive wealth levels, take \(W_{si,-1}=1\), the horizon-zero return equal to wealth minus one, and all later returns zero.  This verifies \texttt{def:buyhold-level}, consistency, event-date transport, the two query-conditional design conditions, and all independence restrictions.  Equation (8) of that theorem yields risk at least \(cA\).

The already established construction \texttt{lem:donor-location-two-point-family} supplies two base-class laws with risk at least \(cN^{-\lambda}\).  Its design is independent across calendar dates and independent of its fixed realized paths, so it satisfies the two replacement query-conditional design conditions.  Likewise, for a fixed auxiliary error probability, \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-cluster-two-point-family} supplies two laws in the repaired base class with a common subprobability measure of positive mass and target separation \(cD_T^{1/2}\); its statement expressly enforces the geometric conditional design envelope after replacement of the assumption.  The elementary inequality (8) in \texttt{thm:conditional-frontier} gives risk at least \(cD_T\).  Taking the maximum of the three lower bounds and using (4) proves
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}
 \mathbb E_P[\{\widetilde\tau-\tau(z_0)\}^2\mid z_0]
 \asymp A\vee D_T\vee N^{-\lambda}\asymp R_\star.
\tag{5}
\]

On \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{iid}}_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), the last part of \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-anchor-moment} replaces \(D_T\) in (2) by \(T^{-2\lambda/d}\).  For the converse, choose a conditionally independent uniform design, take a cube of radius \(r_T=cT^{-1/d}\) about \(z_{01}\), and use two bounded Holder surfaces that agree outside the cube and differ at its center by \(c_1r_T^\lambda\).  The hit probability \(p_T\) is at most \(v_dr_T^d\) at each date.  Conditional calendar independence and a sufficiently small fixed \(c\) give
\[
 \Pr\{X_{1t}\text{ misses the cube for all }t\mid z_0\}
 =(1-p_T)^T\ge c_2>0.
\tag{6}
\]
Restricted to this event, the two observed response laws coincide while the targets differ by \(c_1T^{-\lambda/d}\).  Their common subprobability measure and (8) prove the lower squared-risk term \(cT^{-2\lambda/d}\).

Remain on this conditionally independent-calendar subclass and set \(S=1\), \(H=0\), \(p=d=1\), and \(n_1=n\).  The unreduced upper bookkeeping terms are
\[
 n^{-1}\vee(Tn)^{-2\lambda/(2\lambda+1)}\vee T^{-2\lambda}\vee N^{-\lambda}.
\]
Equation (4) shows that the smoothing term is dominated by the maximum of the first and third terms.  This proves the three nonredundant phases and the displayed oracle/generated-proxy boundary.

Lemma \texttt{lem:causal-identification} gives the observed-law functional, and bounded wealth gives \(\tau(z_0)\in[-2B,2B]\).  We first prove coverage on the regular branch.  Since \(0<\lambda\le1\), one has \(r=0\).  Conditional on the exact design and the donor sample, all selected weights are response-independent, nonnegative, and satisfy \(\sum_t w_{st}=1\).  For each unit history define
\[
 \xi_{si}=\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}\left[
 B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mathbb E(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0)
 -\sum_{t=1}^{T}w_{st}\{Q_{sti}-m_s(X_{st})\}\right].
\tag{1}
\]
By \texttt{ass:donor-training-separation}, the donor sample is conditionally independent of the complete joint panel given \(z_0\).  Therefore conditioning further on the donor sample does not change the conditional law of the unit histories given \((z_0,X)\).  The two equalities in \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering} center (1), and \texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence} makes the \(\xi_{si}\)'s independent across \((s,i)\).  Their range lengths are at most
\[
 d_{si}=\frac{2B\pi_s}{n_s}\left(1+\sum_{t=1}^{T}|w_{st}|\right).
\tag{2}
\]
For a variable \(V\in[a,b]\), convexity of the exponential gives \(\mathbb E\exp\{u(V-\mathbb EV)\}\le\exp\{u^2(b-a)^2/8\}\).  Exponential Markov optimization, independence, and (2) therefore imply
\[
 \Pr\left\{\left|\sum_{s,i}\xi_{si}\right|>r_{\mathrm{unit}}
       \mathrel{\Big|}z_0,X,(Z_j)_j\right\}
 \le2\exp\{-4\log(8/\alpha_{\mathrm{st}})\}
 \le\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}.
\tag{3}
\]
The positive linear term in \(r_{\mathrm{unit}}\) only enlarges the radius.  Notice that (3) treats the complete vector \((Q_{sti})_{t=1}^{T}\) and the event outcome as one bounded unit-history variable; it neither conditions on response blocks nor asserts calendar-score independence.

For the donor event, spectral clipping gives \(\widehat\Sigma\succeq(c_\Sigma/2)I_q\), where \(q=Sd\).  Every fold has size at least \(N/3\), so donor unbiasedness and the upper covariance bound imply
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[N\|\widehat\Sigma^{-1/2}
   (\overline Z_\ell-z_0)\|_2^2\mid z_0\right]
 \le\frac{6qC_\Sigma}{c_\Sigma}.
\tag{4}
\]
This uses only the deterministic eigenvalue bound on the clipped matrix and does not require independence between the sample mean and covariance estimate.  Markov's inequality, a union bound over at most two folds, and the definition of \(q_{\mathrm{don}}\) give
\[
 \Pr\left\{\max_\ell\|\widehat\Sigma^{-1/2}
  (\overline Z_\ell-z_0)\|_2>q_{\mathrm{don}}N^{-1/2}\mid z_0\right\}
 \le\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{5}
\]
On the complement, the upper clipping bound and nonexpansiveness of cube projection imply \(\max_\ell\|\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\|_2\le CN^{-1/2}\).  At any selected local-constant fit, nonnegative unit-mass weights and kernel support give
\[
 \left|\sum_t w_{st}^{(\ell)}m_s(X_{st})-m_s(\widetilde z_{\ell s})\right|
 \le C\{\|\widehat u_{s\ell}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\lambda
           +\widehat h_{s\ell}^\lambda\}.
\tag{6}
\]
Holder continuity between \(\widetilde z_{\ell s}\) and \(z_{0s}\), (5), and the defining domination property of \(C_H\) show that the total deterministic error is at most \(r_{\mathrm{bias}}+r_{\mathrm{don}}\).  Combining (3), (5), and \(\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}+\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}=\alpha\) proves coverage on the regular branch.  On every declared bad branch \(C_\alpha=[-2B,2B]\), which contains the target.  Intersecting a covering interval with this known target range preserves coverage.  Thus the displayed asymptotic uniform coverage follows; no calendar-score radius is used.

We next bound expected length.  On the regular branch, \(\sum_t|w_{st}|=1\), whence
\[
 r_{\mathrm{samp}}=r_{\mathrm{unit}}\le C(\alpha,B)A^{1/2},
 \qquad A=\sum_s\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}.
\tag{7}
\]
Indeed, the square-root term is immediate and \(\max_s\pi_s/n_s\le A^{1/2}\).  Whenever the reference anchor is available, selected-certificate optimality gives
\[
 r_{\mathrm{bias}}
 \le C\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\left\{(h_s^\star)^\lambda
 +K_N^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K_N}\|\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\|_2^\lambda\right\}.
\tag{8}
\]
Donor unbiasedness, ellipticity, projection nonexpansiveness, and Jensen's inequality yield
\[
 \mathbb E(\|\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\|_2^\lambda\mid z_0)
 \le CN^{-\lambda/2}.
\tag{9}
\]
Taking expectations in (8) and applying the query-conditional moment bound \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-anchor-moment} gives
\[
\begin{split}
 \sup_P\mathbb E_P(r_{\mathrm{bias}}+r_{\mathrm{don}}\mid z_0)
 \le C\bigg[&\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s(Tn_s)^{-\lambda/(2\lambda+d)}
 +\left\{\frac{\log(T\vee2)}T\right\}^{\lambda/d}
 +N^{-\lambda/2}\bigg].
\end{split}
\tag{10}
\]
Along the stated growth arrays the deterministic small-sample branches disappear.  The fixed-scale part of the anchor lemma bounds the remaining unavailable-reference event by \(CT^{-2}\); interval length is always at most \(4B\).  Equations (7)--(10) and the smoothing domination in \texttt{thm:marginal-phase-diagram} imply
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}
 \mathbb E_P\{\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)\mid z_0\}
 \le CR_\star^{1/2}.
\tag{11}
\]
On \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{iid}}_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), the independent part of the anchor lemma replaces the logarithmic term by \(T^{-\lambda/d}\).

For the converse, suppose two laws with targets \(\theta_0,\theta_1\) possess a common subprobability measure \(\nu\) of mass \(\eta>2\alpha\).  Uniform conditional coverage \(1-\alpha-o(1)\) under both laws gives
\[
 \nu\{\theta_0,\theta_1\in I_\alpha\}\ge\eta-2\alpha-o(1).
\]
Every interval on this event has length at least \(|\theta_1-\theta_0|\), and therefore
\[
 \max_{v=0,1}\mathbb E_v\operatorname{length}(I_\alpha)
 \ge|\theta_1-\theta_0|\{\eta-2\alpha-o(1)\}.
\tag{12}
\]
Embed the treated pair (9)--(10) of \texttt{thm:conditional-frontier} in the causal class using query-conditionally independent uniform designs, constant untreated surfaces, an admissible common donor law independent of the complete panel, and positive translated event outcomes, exactly as in the treated-channel construction of \texttt{thm:marginal-phase-diagram}.  This verifies the replacement design assumptions, consistency, event-date transport, and the buy-and-hold representation.  Choose \(\gamma\) small enough that the pair's common mass exceeds \(2\alpha\); (12) then gives \(cA^{1/2}\).

added_lemmas.statement:
Put \(q=Sd\).  Suppose \(\delta_0<1/2\), \(B^4>q^2\), \(c_\Sigma I_q\preceq\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_q\), and \(\operatorname{dist}(z_{0s},\partial[0,1]^d)\ge\delta_0\) for every \(s\).  For every \(\eta\in(0,1)\), there are constants \(c_\eta>0\) and \(N_\eta<\infty\), depending only on \(\eta\) and the fixed class parameters, such that for every \(N\ge N_\eta\) there are probability laws \(G_0,G_1\) on \(\mathbb R^q\) with means \(z_0,z_1\), respectively, common covariance \(\Sigma\), and
\[
 \mathbb E_{G_v}\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z-z_v)\|_2^4\le B^4,
 \qquad
 N\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(z_1-z_0)\|_2^2=c_\eta^2,
 \qquad v\in\{0,1\}.
\]
The displacement \(z_1-z_0\) has one nonzero coordinate, \(z_1\) obeys the same \(\delta_0\)-interior restriction, and the product laws satisfy \(\|G_1^{\otimes N}-G_0^{\otimes N}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le1-\eta\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Let \(q=Sd\), and choose a coordinate vector \(e\) with sign pointing from the corresponding coordinate of \(z_0\) toward \(1/2\).  A displacement \(ve\) with \(0\le v\le1/2-\delta_0\) therefore remains in the \(\delta_0\)-trimmed cube.  Put
\[
 w=\frac{\Sigma^{-1/2}e}{\|\Sigma^{-1/2}e\|_2}
\]
and choose an orthogonal matrix \(O\) sending the first coordinate vector to \(w\).  Fix
\[
 0<\epsilon< B^4-q^2,
 \qquad c_0=(1+\epsilon)^{1/2}.
\]
For a real number \(u\) near zero, define a scalar random variable \(A_u\) on \(\{-c_0,0,c_0\}\) by
\[
 p_+(u)=\frac{1+u^2}{2c_0^2}+\frac{u}{2c_0},\qquad
 p_-(u)=\frac{1+u^2}{2c_0^2}-\frac{u}{2c_0},\qquad
 p_0(u)=1-\frac{1+u^2}{c_0^2}.
\tag{1}
\]
At \(u=0\) all three probabilities are strictly positive.  Hence they remain probabilities for \(|u|\le u_0\), for some \(u_0>0\).  Direct calculation from (1) gives
\[
 \mathbb E A_u=u,
 \qquad \mathbb E A_u^2=1+u^2,
 \qquad \operatorname{Var}(A_u)=1.
\tag{2}
\]
Let \(R_2,\ldots,R_q\) be independent Rademacher variables, independent of \(A_u\), and set
\[
 V_u=O(A_u,R_2,\ldots,R_q)^{\top}.
\]
Equations (1)--(2) imply
\[
 \mathbb EV_u=uw,\qquad \operatorname{Var}(V_u)=I_q.
\tag{3}
\]
Orthogonal invariance of Euclidean norm and independence give
\[
 \mathbb E\|V_u-uw\|_2^4
 =\mathbb E(A_u-u)^4+2(q-1)+(q-1)^2.
\tag{4}
\]
At \(u=0\), the right side of (4) is \(c_0^2+q^2-1=q^2+\epsilon<B^4\).  It is continuous in \(u\), so, after decreasing \(u_0\), it is at most \(B^4\) whenever \(|u|\le u_0\).

Define \(G_u\) as the law of
\[
 Z_u=z_0+\Sigma^{1/2}V_u.
\]
By (3), its mean and covariance are
\[
 z(u)=z_0+u\Sigma^{1/2}w
     =z_0+\frac{u}{\|\Sigma^{-1/2}e\|_2}e,
 \qquad \operatorname{Var}(Z_u)=\Sigma,
\tag{5}
\]
and (4) is exactly the required standardized fourth moment about \(z(u)\).

It remains to control overlap.  The Hellinger affinity between \(G_0\) and \(G_u\) equals
\[
 a(u)=\sum_{r\in\{-,0,+\}}\{p_r(0)p_r(u)\}^{1/2},
\]
because the Rademacher coordinates, the rotation, and the invertible linear transformation are common.  On a sufficiently small compact neighborhood of zero, the three square-root terms have bounded second derivatives.  Moreover, \(a(0)=1\) and
\[
 a'(0)=\frac12\sum_r p_r'(0)=0.
\]
Taylor's theorem therefore gives \(a(u)\ge1-Cu^2\).  For \(CNu^2\le1/2\),
\[
 a(u)^N\ge(1-Cu^2)^N\ge\exp(-2CNu^2).
\tag{6}
\]
For any two dominated laws with densities \(p,g\), Cauchy--Schwarz applied to \(|p-g|=|\sqrt p-\sqrt g|(\sqrt p+\sqrt g)\) yields
\[
 \|P-G\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le\left\{1-\left(\int\sqrt{pg}\right)^2\right\}^{1/2}.
\tag{7}
\]
Choose \(c_\eta>0\) small enough that the right side of (7), after using (6) with \(u=c_\eta N^{-1/2}\), is at most \(1-\eta\).  Also take \(c_\eta\le1\).  Equations (5)--(7) then give
\[
 \|G_{c_\eta N^{-1/2}}^{\otimes N}-G_0^{\otimes N}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le1-\eta,\qquad
 N\|\Sigma^{-1/2}\{z(c_\eta N^{-1/2})-z_0\}\|_2^2=c_\eta^2.
\]
Finally, ellipticity gives \(\|\Sigma^{-1/2}e\|_2^{-1}\le C_\Sigma^{1/2}\).  Thus (5) remains in the trimmed cube for all sufficiently large \(N\).  Taking \(G_0=G_{u=0}\), \(G_1=G_{u=c_\eta N^{-1/2}}\), and enlarging \(N_\eta\) to enforce all preceding bounds proves the lemma.

proposed.name: Total unit-history concentration interval
proposed.construction:
Put \(\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}=\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}=\alpha/2\).  On the regular branch, let \(w_{st}\) be the actual response weight obtained by averaging the selected foldwise intercept weights, and define
\[
 A_w=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\frac{\pi_s^2}{n_s}
       \left(1+\sum_{t=1}^{T}|w_{st}|\right)^2,
 \qquad
 M_w=\max_{1\le s\le S}\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}
       \left(1+\sum_{t=1}^{T}|w_{st}|\right).
\]
The unit-history sampling radius is
\[
 r_{\mathrm{unit}}
 =B\{8A_w\log(8/\alpha_{\mathrm{st}})\}^{1/2}
  +\frac{8B}{3}M_w\log(8/\alpha_{\mathrm{st}}),
 \qquad r_{\mathrm{samp}}=r_{\mathrm{unit}}.
\]
For \(N\ge2\), form the sample covariance of the donor scores and spectrally clip it to \([c_\Sigma/2,2C_\Sigma]\), as in the definition of \(\widehat\Sigma\), and put
\[
 q_{\mathrm{don}}
 =\left\{\frac{32SdC_\Sigma}{c_\Sigma\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}}\right\}^{1/2}.
\]
Define
\[
 r_{\mathrm{bias}}
 =C_H\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_sK_N^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^{K_N}
 \left(\|\widehat u_{s\ell}-\widetilde z_{\ell s}\|_2^\kappa
       +\widehat h_{s\ell}^{\lambda}\right),
 \qquad
 r_{\mathrm{don}}=C_H(q_{\mathrm{don}}/\sqrt N)^\kappa,
\]
and
\[
 R_\alpha=r_{\mathrm{samp}}+r_{\mathrm{bias}}+r_{\mathrm{don}},
 \qquad
 C_\alpha=[\widehat\tau-R_\alpha,\widehat\tau+R_\alpha]\cap[-2B,2B].
\]
If \(N<2\), some \(n_s<2\), a candidate set \(\mathcal A_{s\ell}\) is empty, or any numerical input is undefined or nonfinite, set \(C_\alpha=[-2B,2B]\).  Thus the procedure is total, uses only unit-history bounded-range concentration for its sampling radius, and never divides by an estimated variance.

prose_updates.interpretation: Conditionally, exact-site geometry and a generated donor query are separate sources of difficulty.  Query-conditional density and design mixing ensure that a realized event path cannot systematically select an unregulated design hole, so occupancy converts fixed-design ambiguity into the geometric-mixing spacing rate.  Donor uncertainty dominates when \(N^{-\lambda}\) exceeds treated replication and spacing. prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The no-deconvolution conclusion relies on exact historical paths, and every constructive headline is restricted to \(0<\lambda\le1\). Geometric conditional design mixing retains the logarithmic spacing penalty; only conditional design independence yields the no-log term. prose_updates.honest_scope: Event-date transport is an untestable causal restriction.  Query-conditional density and design mixing are observed-law design restrictions, while design-conditional centering is a separate response sampling condition.  Donor-panel separation factors donors from the complete joint panel conditional on the query and leaves dependence within each unit's training-event history unrestricted.  Risk, coverage, and expected-length upper bounds hold over the base rough-Holder class without a lower local modulus.  The interval uses no calendar-score branch or estimated-variance division.  The donor converse needs strict interior and fourth-moment slack.  Higher smoothness, growing dimension, adaptation, uniform-in-query bands, and exact constants are outside scope.
